edges.description: Clonal expansion of transformed hepatocytes into a tumor mass enlarges the liver and can produce a palpable, nodular hepatomegaly.
Tumor growth stretches the hepatic capsule and may cause tumor necrosis, producing right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
The growing malignancy drives cancer cachexia and decreased appetite, producing unintentional weight loss.
Advanced tumor burden together with underlying hepatic dysfunction produces profound fatigue.
Progressive tumor growth causing biliary obstruction and loss of hepatic synthetic/excretory function produces jaundice in advanced disease.
Tumor-associated portal hypertension and hypoalbuminemia from impaired hepatic synthesis produce ascites in advanced disease.
Tumor-cell IL-6 promotes M2-like macrophage polarization.

nodes.description: Inducible phase II enzymes detoxify reactive aflatoxin metabolites and compete with DNA-adduct formation. Reduced GSTM1 capacity can therefore modify susceptibility, while oltipraz can induce this protective route.

evidence.reference_title: Chemoprevention of hepatocellular carcinoma in aflatoxin endemic areas.
evidence.snippet: oltipraz, is a potent inducer of phase 2 enzymes involved in the detoxication of carcinogens including aflatoxin.

nodes.description: The reactive AFB1-8,9-exo-epoxide binds covalently to genomic DNA, forming pro-mutagenic AFB1-N7-guanine adducts preferentially at guanine residues. This adduct is the DNA lesion that bridges metabolic activation to the characteristic TP53 codon 249 transversion.

evidence.reference_title: Epigenetic alterations caused by aflatoxin b1: a public health risk in the induction of hepatocellular carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: which interacts with DNA to form adducts of AFB1-DNA. These adducts induce mutation in codon 249, mediated by a transversion of G-T in the p53 tumor suppressor gene

nodes.description: In experimental HCC systems, AFB1 exposure activates NF-kappa B-dependent IL-6 expression in tumor cells, providing a disease-specific route by which aflatoxin can remodel the immune microenvironment.

nodes.description: AFB1 is absorbed from the gut and transported to the liver where it undergoes cytochrome P450-mediated oxidation (primarily CYP3A4 and CYP1A2) to form AFB1-8,9-epoxide, a highly reactive electrophilic metabolite. This CYP-dependent bioactivation step is the proximal event that converts the parent mycotoxin into its DNA-reactive form.

evidence.snippet: Lymphoblast microsomes expressing only CYP1A2 activated AFB1 to AFB1-8,9-epoxide (AFB1-8,9-epoxide trapped as the glutathione, conjugate) at both 16 microM and 128 microM AFB1 concentrations

nodes.description: CDK4 phosphorylation promotes PIN1-dependent nuclear localization of TP53 R249S, which interacts with c-Myc and increases c-Myc-dependent ribosomal biogenesis and HCC-cell proliferation.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide association study of the TP53 R249S mutation in hepatocellular carcinoma with aflatoxin B1 exposure and infection with hepatitis B virus.
evidence.snippet: Exposure to dietary aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) induces DNA damage and mutation in the TP53 gene at codon 249, known as the TP53 R249S mutation, and is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

nodes.description: The aflatoxin-DNA adduct forms preferentially at the third position of codon 249 in TP53, causing a G>T transversion that results in arginine-to-serine substitution (R249S). This mutation is enriched in HCCs from high-aflatoxin regions but is rare in low-exposure areas. The R249S mutation impairs p53 DNA binding and transcriptional activity, eliminating its tumor suppressor function.

evidence.reference_title: The aflatoxin-induced TP53 mutation at codon 249 (R249S): biomarker of exposure, early detection and target for therapy.
evidence.snippet: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) in high-incidence areas (sub-Saharan Africa, South-Eastern Asia) often contains a somatic mutation at codon 249 in TP53 (R249S). This mutation is rare in low-incidence areas of Europe and the United States.

nodes.description: TP53 R249S and HBx jointly support proliferation and clonal expansion of transformed hepatocytes in experimental HCC cell systems.

evidence.snippet: in a cell line that constitutively expresses both p.R249S and the hepatitis B virus antigen HBx (PLC/PRF/5), silencing of either p.R249S or HBx by RNA interference slowed down proliferation
